A separate product-state positive control achieves MAE 0.007755 versus 0.514811 for zero, but does not explain the failure on the entangled workload. The difference between zero and a training-fitted mean constant under training MSE is only 0.14%, a descriptive point estimate without uncertainty analysis. The transformer's 815,233-parameter source identity is locally verified; detailed packed-input semantics have not been independently audited. These results constitute a descriptive pilot, not a causal explanation, formal equivalence test, or impossibility claim. Comparable circuits can be regenerated from the workload specification, but exact frozen datasets and model-run evidence remain private.

arxiv:2611.19999.title: MOBO-CAPS: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization with Cardinality-Aware Pareto Selection
arxiv:2611.19999.abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) traditionally aims to approximate the entire Pareto front, but, due to resource constraints, real-world deployment is often limited to testing a small, representative subset of solutions. Hence current methods first approximate the full front before selecting solutions, potentially wasting costly evaluations. We formalize this problem as Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Cardinality-aware Pareto Selection (MOBO-CAPS), where the goal is to identify a set of exactly M solutions with high hypervolume. We propose two practical cardinality-aware acquisition strategies: REHVI, a replacement-aware approximation to expected hypervolume improvement, and CHO-UCB, which constructs an optimistic M-point set by optimizing a collective UCB-based hypervolume objective. We prove a sublinear simple regret bound for the batched version of CHO-UCB, and empirically show that cardinality-aware acquisition design improves over standard MOBO followed by post-hoc subset selection across nine benchmarks.

arxiv:2611.20019.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
arxiv:2611.20019.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. At the local level, for 47 decisions shortly before a failure of SKIP or NEUTRALIZE, removing or neutralizing a small group of bad experiences, with a median size of one, caused the trained agent to select the failing policy's action in 46 cases. For this agent, the results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

arxiv:2611.20020.title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
arxiv:2611.20020.abstract: This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures. We present four main contributions. First, we characterize the generic expressive power of geometric message-passing neural networks on sparse graphs and introduce EGenNet, an architecture achieving the corresponding guarantees. Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture combining strong expressivity and bi-Lipschitz stability guarantees with strong empirical performance on long-range graph-learning tasks. Together, these results provide a broader understanding of how neural architectures can preserve the geometric, algebraic, order-theoretic, and metric structure of their inputs.

arxiv:2611.20036.title: Machine Learning for Near Real-Time Identification of Wildfire Burned Areas
arxiv:2611.20036.abstract: In this article, we present a near real-time method that estimates burned probability anywhere in the world using satellite images. Our approach takes advantage of the state-of-the-art pix2pix model to translate a preprocessed index calculated from Landsat 8/9 images into an approximate of USGS Burn Probability indicating per pixel burn probability. Since this is a machine learning-based approach, it can be automated with a minimum amount of human intervention with significantly less time delays and geographic restrictions compared to other contemporary methods. We include results from our experiments and compare our approximation with the USGS Burn Probability using RMSE score.

arxiv:2611.20060.title: Communication-Efficient Distributionally Robust Federated Averaging with Multi-Source Data
arxiv:2611.20060.abstract: Federated learning trains a shared model from distributed client data. The deployment risk is typically specified through two approximations: each unknown local distribution is replaced by its empirical distribution, and the unknown deployment mixture across clients is replaced by empirical or prescribed training weights. Existing robust methods usually address one approximation at a time through local distributional ambiguity sets or worst-case client mixtures. However, joint treatment of both approximations remains underexplored. To address this gap, we construct a global ambiguity set formed by admissible mixtures of client-wise Wasserstein ambiguity sets, yielding a distributionally robust optimization formulation. The construction allows client-dependent ambiguity radii, preserves client-wise separability of the objective function, and yields a high-probability out-of-sample guarantee for the resulting robust problem. We then introduce a penalty-based approximation of this formulation and develop a communication-efficient algorithm called BiDRO-FedAvg, for which we establish a convergence guarantee. We validate the proposed framework through a market-demand prediction simulation.

arxiv:2611.20064.title: Decode Early, Verify Late: Streaming Offline Speech Recognizers Without Accuracy Loss
arxiv:2611.20064.abstract: Voice agents need accurate transcripts soon after a user stops speaking. We propose Decode Early, Verify Late (DEVL), a training-free framework for streaming inference with offline ASR models. The server keeps partial transcripts as drafts and verifies the latest against the complete audio in one forward pass at turn end. Under stated input and decoding conditions, the final equals the model's greedy offline output in exact arithmetic. We adapt DEVL to four model families. In our five-recognizer comparison, 95-100% of final transcripts are byte-identical to the offline transcripts, WER stays within 0.13 points of offline, and single-stream time to final falls 1.5-7.3x. Serving Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on one A100, DEVL returns finals a median 22-26 ms after turn end at up to 64 streams, 2.7-3.9x sooner than the official streaming mode. It is the only system we tested that meets a 100 ms p99 target, up to 80 streams on Pipecat-STT and 64 on WildASR.

arxiv:2611.20078.title: Infrastructure-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Attention for Highway Ramp Merging
arxiv:2611.20078.abstract: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. Without proper coordination, human drivers and self-interested autonomous vehicles may make risky manoeuvres and cause accidents or congestion. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging. However, in dense traffic, forming an effective observation of the traffic state is challenging. For example, observing only the neighbouring vehicles may lead to locally optimal decisions, while observing the entire traffic can introduce much irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based MARL vehicle control model to address these problems. A roadside infrastructure controller receives the states of all CAVs via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication and sends control commands back to them. An attention-based observation encoder is designed where each vehicle can filter the relevant vehicle information from the global traffic state. The proposed model is evaluated in SUMO against three baselines: a model that observes only the neighbouring vehicles, a model that encodes the global traffic information, and the rule-based SUMO model. The results show that our model achieves the highest traffic flow, safety and smoothness. Furthermore, in a four-hour simulation with dynamic traffic demand, our model successfully avoids traffic jams, while other baseline models fail at high traffic flow. We also show that our model remains effective when human-driven vehicles are present. We further show that our model, trained in ideal communication conditions, can still remain collision-free and maintain throughput under realistic V2I communication errors. Finally, we visualise the relevance weights that an ego vehicle assigns to other vehicles in multiple traffic situations.

arxiv:2611.20087.title: Does Learning Order Explain Forgetting? The Lie Bracket as an Early-Warning Signal for Catastrophic Forgetting Without Old Data
arxiv:2611.20087.abstract: A network trained on task A and then task B ends at different weights than one trained on B and then A. To leading order this gap is set by the Lie bracket of the two tasks' gradient fields, and Dherin (2023) conjectured that a non-vanishing bracket may be linked to catastrophic forgetting. I test this conjecture empirically. Across Split MNIST, Split Fashion-MNIST and Split CIFAR-10, the forgetting of A is almost exactly the difference in A's loss between the two training orders (Spearman rho = 0.96-1.00). I then ask whether the bracket can predict that forgetting early in training on B and without any of A's data, using only a small summary stored when A finishes: its gradient and its top 20 Hessian eigenpairs. When the old task is well learned and forgetting is slow (task-incremental), this stored bracket ranks forgetting with rho = 0.70-0.81, against 0.33-0.58 for the penalty of Elastic Weight Consolidation, and matches or exceeds re-evaluating A on its own data. When forgetting is fast (domain-incremental), the stored summary goes stale and the EWC penalty is as good or better. The bracket fails outright when the old task is only half learned; I trace this to a residual gradient on A an order of magnitude larger, which makes first-order (slope) damage matter. The bracket is therefore a useful early-warning signal for the quiet kind of forgetting, under a clear condition.

arxiv:2611.20109.title: MT-RGCN-DTI: A Multi-Task Relational Graph Convolutional Network for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
arxiv:2611.20109.abstract: Prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) has become a very crucial part of drug discovery. With the increase in the data volume, it has become very important to improve prediction accuracy by integrating multiple data sources. In this regard, utilising multiple resources in the form of heterogeneous information network to address DTI prediction can be rewarding. In this work, we propose a heterogeneous information network based multi-task DTI prediction model which leverages the advantages of relation graph convolutional network (RGCN). To achieve this, the model employs drug-target interaction network, drug-drug similarity network and protein-protein similarity network to construct a heterogeneous information network. Moreover, we use a knowledge graph embedding scoring functions to model interactions between drug and targets, specifically DistMult and ComplEx as decoders over the learned node representations. We performed extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods. We observed that the proposed model shows competitive performance, thereby confirming the effectiveness of our approach. The codes and datasets are available at https://github.com/Dheeran-S/MT-RGCN-DTI/.

arxiv:2611.20119.title: CECAR: Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing Accelerates On-Device Inference of MoE LLMs
arxiv:2611.20119.abstract: Despite growing interest in on-device LLM deployment, large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models remain impractical on resource-constrained devices, as sparse expert activation still requires all expert weights to be memory-resident. To address this, we identify three key observations for on-device MoE inference: (a) cache hit rates are fundamentally bounded even under Belady's optimal policy; (b) these bounds are insufficient for low-latency on-device inference; and (c) prior cache-aware routing based on binary cache presence can induce routing instability. Based on these insights, we propose CECAR (Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing), a MoE inference system that jointly considers expert routing and cache management. Unlike prior cache-aware routing methods, CECAR uses an ML-based cache policy to predict the expected reuse distance of each expert and prioritizes routing and execution toward experts with smaller predicted reuse distances. On the Qwen3-30B-A3B model, CECAR achieves 12.5 tokens/s on a consumer-grade GPU with only 16 GB of VRAM, where non-resident experts are fetched from SSD, delivering a 4.5x speedup over conventional MoE inference and exceeding the decode speed of baselines that keep the entire model fully resident in DRAM. Code is available at https://github.com/hoonki2002/CECAR.

arxiv:2611.20124.title: QA-CMIF:Accurate and Lightweight Cross-Modal Latent Imputation and Fusion for Fault-Tolerant sEMG-Inertial Hand Gesture Recognition
arxiv:2611.20124.abstract: Fusing surface electromyography (sEMG) with inertial measurements is widely used for myoelectric prosthesis control and wearable human-machine interfaces. In daily wear, however, socket micro-displacement, electrode lift-off, and wire failures often corrupt an unknown subset of sEMG channels through burst artifacts, lift-off shocks, or open-circuit dropouts. Existing fusion networks mix all channels in the first convolutional layer, so a few corrupted electrodes contaminate the entire latent representation, whereas gate-only attenuation of corrupted channels discards the co-activation cues needed to separate fine-grained gestures. We propose QA-CMIF, a quality-aware cross-modal latent imputation and fusion framework that encodes each sEMG channel independently, scores its reliability with a soft gate, and protects intact channels via a confidence-weighted residual bypass, while a cross-attention imputer repairs degraded channels in latent space using the inertial stream and remaining reliable sEMG channels under a bad-channel alignment loss. Across within-subject evaluations on 29 participants from Ninapro DB3, DB2, and DB5 spanning 17-52 gesture classes, QA-CMIF outperformed the gate-only baseline under 50% channel corruption by 1.29-2.65 percentage points, denoted pp, across all three 17-class cohorts with paired-t Holm-adjusted p<0.002, widened this margin to 2.59-4.15 pp on the 40- and 52-class tasks, and surpassed corruption-augmented conventional fusion by 4.61-19.85 pp. Requiring only 0.175-0.185M parameters and 2.45-2.63M multiply-accumulate operations across the 2000 Hz and 200 Hz setups, QA-CMIF saves 46%-55% in parameters and 72%-81% in compute over recent baselines with a 1.44 ms 99th-percentile single-thread CPU latency.

arxiv:2611.20150.title: Symmetry Fingerprinting with Geometric Learnable Invariants Transformers
arxiv:2611.20150.abstract: Geometric deep learning has made available a large variety of structurally equivariant neural network architectures, meaning a particular transformation of their input causes a predictable transformation of their output. But structural equivariance is a very strong inductive bias that can limit performance if chosen poorly. In contrast, choosing an architecture with low geometric bias necessitates data augmentation to obtain correct behavior; extending the training process. We propose a novel neural network architecture that is soft equivariant; we select a set of symmetry groups and during training the network will become equivariant only to those symmetry groups that are appropriate given the training data. After training we can inspect the network to obtain a symmetry fingerprint that will tell us exactly which symmetries ended up being relevant and to what degree. We show how our architecture and the fingerprinting process work in the case of an image classification task.

arxiv:2611.20174.title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
arxiv:2611.20174.abstract: Neural networks are typically programmed through optimization, rather than by explicitly specifying their computations. Recent work on weight-space programming suggests that large language models (LLMs) can instead reason about and manipulate neural-network weights directly. In this work, we show that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets. We investigate three complementary settings using GPT-6 Astra, without gradient-based optimization. First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from zero-initialized weights, achieving a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared to 0.876 for a pretrained baseline. Second, Astra diagnoses and repairs a signed-product regression failure in pretrained TabPFN-3.5, restoring near-perfect predictions on held-out synthetic datasets while preserving performance on TabArena-Lite, with only a 0.08% average relative increase in error. Third, it writes KV-cache-editing programs that steer TabPFN-3.5's predictions on unseen synthetic datasets, demonstrating transformations such as reversing linear trends and converting sine waves into approximate square waves, without modifying model weights. Together, our findings suggest that LLM-driven programming could complement gradient-based optimization across TFMs' development and usage, while offering a new way to investigate and intervene in their internal computations.

arxiv:2611.20180.title: UrbanROI: Causal Modeling for Regional ROI Forecasting under POI Entry
arxiv:2611.20180.abstract: As urban commercial environments continue to evolve rapidly, accurately modeling the economic impact of point of interest (POI) entry is essential for supporting data-driven advertising allocation, merchant onboarding, and regional business decision-making. Existing return on investment (ROI) prediction methods mainly focus on individual ads or merchants, overlooking the interaction effects among POIs and failing to capture the causal influence of structural changes in urban commercial ecosystems. In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- regional ROI forecasting under POI entry, which aims to predict the future ROI trajectory of a commercial region after the introduction of a new POI by modeling temporal ROI evolution and competition-driven interactions among surrounding POIs. To address these challenges, we propose UrbanROI, an intervention-aware causal forecasting framework for region-level economic outcome prediction. UrbanROI leverages an Interaction-aware Regional Graph Module to explicitly model competitive relationships among POIs based on user request contexts, spatial proximity, and request-level commercial signals, and constructs structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to simulate factual and counterfactual regional states. Extensive experiments on large-scale real-world POI and advertising datasets demonstrate that UrbanROI consistently outperforms strong baselines in post-entry regional ROI forecasting. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in temporal economic modeling, inter-POI interaction representation, and intervention-aware forecasting, providing support for regional economic analysis and business decision-making in dynamic urban commercial systems.

arxiv:2611.20255.title: Deep Sequence Model for Genome Wide Discovery of Coding and Regulatory Element Signatures
arxiv:2611.20255.abstract: Interpreting deep neural networks for genomic sequence classification remains challenging despite strong predictive performance. We develop a lightweight CNN with post-training gradient-based analysis to identify which sequence positions drive coding versus intergenomic classification. Applied to the standardized demo_coding_vs_intergenomic_seqs dataset, our model achieves 91.87% validation accuracy while revealing interpretable patterns: nine hot spots with consistently high importance, clear class-specific separation at positions 20-100 (coding) and 150-190 (intergenomic), and a strong mean-variance correlation (r = 0.530) indicating robust discriminative features. Gradient-based importance analysis shows that the model implicitly learns biologically meaningful sequence distinctions without explicit annotations. This work demonstrates that neural network interpretability and accuracy can coexist, providing a framework for understanding genomic sequence classification and enabling biology-driven hypothesis generation.

arxiv:2611.20258.title: Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
arxiv:2611.20258.abstract: Continual learning is a promising approach to specialize language models to an organization's private data. However, current methods exhibit a number of drawbacks including catastrophic forgetting, where new training updates overwrite prior knowledge. We present microfitting, which trains and caches a small adapter for each document. Each adapter is trained once, offline, on synthetic questions targeted at demonstrated base-model shortcomings and reused whenever that document is queried. This method borrows from test-time learning literature and sidesteps the problem of continual learning through parameter isolation, allowing the system to specialize on new data without overwriting prior knowledge. The process that generates adapter training data also improves over time, revising its recipe from previous outcomes and fresh examples of the target workload. On DeepSeek V4 Flash, microfitting substantially improves accuracy over the base model. In Enterprise Document Operations (EDO), an open-book Q&A environment over real-world enterprise documents, our method achieves a 38.2% relative improvement over base-model performance. Microfitting makes continual specialization practical and cost-efficient: a frozen model can adapt to an evolving private corpus overnight on local hardware, without modifying the base model or previously cached adapters.

arxiv:2611.20259.title: Scaling large language model-assisted line-of-therapy adjudication with human-in-the-loop evidence-calibrated selection
arxiv:2611.20259.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled the ability to scale clinical adjudication tasks traditionally dependent on exhaustive manual review. Line-of-therapy (LoT) adjudication, a major bottleneck in oncology cohort construction, is a prime example. Line boundaries must be inferred from longitudinal treatment histories according to nuanced, study-specific definitions, at every regimen transition for every patient. LLMs can apply this adjudication at scale, but their reliability varies across patients. Treatment histories differ in complexity, and ambiguous or atypical patterns depend on expert clinical judgment. Reliable automation thus requires verified support for model assignments and the ability to identify cases that warrant manual review. Here, we present evidence-calibrated selection (ECS), a human-in-the-loop framework for scaling LLM-assisted LoT adjudication. ECS derives confidence from observed clinician adjudications, prioritizes patients with the least-supported assignments for follow-up review, and returns completed adjudications to the model as precedent. As the evidence base grows, ECS continuously calibrates confidence to estimate residual error, thus enabling more efficient use of clinician time. In simulations on 136 clinician adjudicated patients with multiple myeloma, ECS achieved a residual error of 5% after review of 44.6% of patients, compared to 62.2% when review was directed by LLM self-reported confidence and 81.9% under random sampling. These results support a scalable approach to study-specific LoT adjudication, using clinician evidence to inform automated predictions, minimize error, and reduce review burden.

arxiv:2611.20261.title: Estimating Outpatient Visit Prices from Hospital Price Transparency Data using Large Language Models
arxiv:2611.20261.abstract: Objective: Hospital care prices in the United States have increased substantially, yet patients lack effective tools to access and compare costs. We aimed to develop and evaluate an LLM-based approach for improving access to and use of hospital price transparency (PT) data. Materials and Methods: To estimate visit prices, we used a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework to analyze PT files from three major hospitals in Maryland and the surrounding region. We compared BM25, OpenAI embedding models, and a GPT-BM25 hybrid against a no-RAG baseline for cost estimation of individual procedures and procedure groups, then evaluated the best approach for symptom-based visit cost estimation using synthetic simulations. Results: Across hospitals, the GPT-BM25 retriever achieved the best performance, with average price MAPE of 19.44% for individual procedures and 4.90% for groups, compared with 147.98% and 82.82%, respectively, for the no-RAG baseline. In simulations, our framework correctly identified approximately 50% of reference procedures and reduced MAPE relative to the LLM-only baseline at two of the three hospitals, while achieving comparable performance at the third. Discussion: Our framework uses RAG to improve care price estimation in real-world settings. Compared with the no-RAG baseline, it substantially improved cost estimates for both individual procedures and procedure groups. Improvements were smaller in synthetic simulations, likely because inferring procedures from clinical information is more complex. Practical challenges remain, including heterogeneous PT file formats, unexplained duplicate entries, and limited availability of insurer-negotiated rates. Conclusion: LLMs that effectively integrate PT data show strong potential to provide patients with more accessible and accurate healthcare cost estimates.

arxiv:2611.20268.title: GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
arxiv:2611.20268.abstract: When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address the action step on a real place. We ask whether a policy can learn the timing of emergency actions from decades of real events. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. On 18 historical test scenarios, PPO achieves a similar reduction in population exposure to the rule. With uncertain forecasts and limited protection it again performs similarly but does not outperform the tuned rule, and removing graph message passing does not substantially reduce performance. PPO therefore learns an effective protective response from an outcome-based reward alone: it is given the plan's actions and when each is allowed, but not the thresholds that tell the comparator when to act. Next steps test harder edge cases, move closer to a digital twin of the territory, and replace the simulated officer with assessment by emergency-management stakeholders, supported by LLM-based interpretation of each recommendation.

arxiv:2611.20288.title: Protecting Safety during Reasoning Training with Low-Rank Fisher Regularisation
arxiv:2611.20288.abstract: Large language models are trained to have safety guardrails, but these can be compromised while fine-tuning for new capabilities, such as reasoning. One way to mitigate this degradation is to modify the fine-tuning objective to preserve safety behaviour, but doing so effectively and efficiently remains challenging. We revisit Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which penalises parameter updates based on sensitivity estimates from the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). While EWC provides some protection, the diagonal approximation ignores interactions between parameters. We address this limitation by exploiting recent findings that safety-relevant behaviour is located in a low-rank subspace within models. Our method, Subspace-Projected Elastic Weight Consolidation (SP-EWC), projects gradients onto this subspace to capture non-diagonal curvature efficiently. We investigate three different ways of identifying the safety subspace: through safety fine-tuning updates (LoRA), safety-related activations (ActSVD), and contrastive representations of safety and utility data (cPCA). We find that this choice substantially affects performance, with SP-EWC using cPCA comparing favourably against existing methods by better maintaining safety guardrails without introducing excessive over-refusal.

arxiv:2611.20331.title: LENS: Replacing LayerNorm and Softmax in Transformers with Learnable Normalization States
arxiv:2611.20331.abstract: LayerNorm and attention Softmax are critical operations in Transformers. However, they cannot be efficiently mapped to General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) computations on hardware. Therefore, modern hardware accelerator designs, such as NPUs on ASIC/FPGA, consume a large amount of hardware resources or chip area to implement their specific arithmetic units. Building on previous work about LayerNorm, Softmax, and their alternatives, we introduce Learnable Normalization States (LENS), a framework that reformulates LayerNorm as tiny MLPs by abstracting a common structure from related methods and extends this method to Softmax, which moves more of the computation in Transformers to GEMM as a hardware-friendly architecture. We evaluate LENS on image classification with Vision Transformers (ViT) and autoregressive language modeling with Pythia models, including generalization tests on WikiText and LAMBADA. Across these tasks, LENS matches or exceeds baseline performance in several vision settings and retains most of the baseline performance in the remaining vision and language experiments. These findings may suggest that hand-designed normalization and attention functions are not the only choice as alternatives to LayerNorm and Softmax. LENS also provides a basis for exploring Transformer architectures for resource-limited accelerators.

arxiv:2611.20334.title: Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
arxiv:2611.20334.abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) models are often trained on nominal data using average-risk objectives, which emphasize dominant normal patterns. However, real time series can contain rare but valid nominal regimes that are underrepresented in the training distribution. We show that data-space flow matching can over-penalize such rare-normal windows and assign them anomaly scores comparable to those of true anomalies. To address this, we propose Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching (RT-FM), an unsupervised framework that uses a temporal variational autoencoder to estimate residual latent tailness and converts it into bounded, warmup-annealed weights for training a data-space flow matching model. Experiments on seven TSAD benchmarks show that RT-FM improves rare-normal coverage while preserving strong anomaly discrimination, substantially reducing false alarms on such windows and resulting in improved aggregate detection performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/trustAIoT/RT-FM_time-series-anomaly

arxiv:2611.20352.title: EPI-SST: Renewal-Structured State-Space Transformers for Epidemic Forecasting
arxiv:2611.20352.abstract: Epidemic forecasting supports public health decisions ranging from capacity planning to intervention timing, for which both point accuracy and calibrated uncertainty are essential. Although neural models have advanced point forecasting, producing reliable probabilistic predictions over multiple future horizons remains challenging. Renewal models encode epidemic propagation, while neural forecasters learn flexible multi-horizon representations; integrating these strengths within a probabilistic future rollout remains underexplored. We propose EPI-SST (Epidemic State Space Transformer), a probabilistic forecaster centered on an evidence-driven renewal transition. At each horizon, neural evidence produces a bounded update to an internal multiplier and advances a finite-memory renewal state that generates the future mean trajectory. A separate heteroscedastic Gaussian head controls predictive scale using a validation-selected log-variance penalty. Across four epidemic surveillance benchmarks, EPI-SST achieves the lowest pooled RMSE on every dataset, reducing RMSE by up to 14.2 percent relative to the strongest baseline. It also achieves the lowest continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at horizons h = 4, 5, 6 on every dataset, with reductions of up to 43 percent relative to the strongest probabilistic baseline. During the abnormal 2019-2020 influenza season, EPI-SST reduces CRPS by 16.9 percent and calibration error by 78.9 percent; a three-seed replication preserves its distributional lead. Ablation studies and frozen-path interventions show that the renewal transition, attention conditioning, horizon coupling, and uncertainty-scale control make complementary contributions to predictive performance.

arxiv:2611.20360.title: Flow Matching for Sampled-Data Control of Angular Distributions
arxiv:2611.20360.abstract: Synchronization and clustering in oscillator networks depend on the joint distribution of the phases. Flow Matching can steer this distribution by learning an angular velocity field from shortest arcs between paired configurations. Each arc is traversed at constant speed, yet the resulting field can vary along its own trajectories. In this article, we study how to control angular transport on the circle and product torus when each controller evaluation selects a rate to hold until the next update. Using the same local velocity samples, Flow Matching learns the instantaneous angular rate and MeanFlow learns its average along the reference trajectory over the control interval. Under direct angular actuation, holding the exact average gives the reference displacement. We relate the displacement error of holding the instantaneous rate and the training residual of MeanFlow to the conditional covariance of the teacher velocities. Experiments with 100 phases show that endpoint pairing affects the comparison. MeanFlow gives smaller one-step errors under minibatch pairing, while permutation alignment reverses the ranking for exchangeable phase clusters.

arxiv:2611.20368.title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
arxiv:2611.20368.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. We present HoloGene, an anisotropic conditional INR framework for estimating continuous 3D gene-expression fields from pre-registered ST sections. Its central contribution is an acquisition-aware factorization that couples dense in-plane synthesis with sparse axial evolution using established GAE, FiLM, pseudo-label supervision, and CORAL components. HoloGene compresses high-dimensional expression profiles into a graph-autoencoder latent manifold, uses pseudo-label-derived signature conditioning to provide coarse intra-section context, and applies depth-dependent FiLM modulation to model axial variation. A signature-stratified correlation-alignment regularizer encourages cross-slice covariance alignment in latent features. Using held-out measured sections as cross-sectional references, HoloGene improves reconstruction accuracy and biological preservation metrics compared with general-purpose INRs and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines. These results support anisotropic conditional modeling as a practical strategy for estimating 3D expression fields from discontinuous ST sections. Code is available at https://github.com/Szym29/HoloGene.

arxiv:2611.20371.title: Pretty Linear Liars: Unregularized Probes Favor Intervention-Unfaithful Features
arxiv:2611.20371.abstract: Linear probing is a common technique in mechanistic interpretability despite the fact that the decodability of a given feature does not necessarily imply the network uses that feature. Intervention faithfulness, not merely decodability, is the appropriate criterion for whether a feature serves a defined active role in the model. Meanwhile, probe regularization has been used for feature discovery, but the impact of regularization on feature causality remains unclear. We study probe regularization systematically, starting with unregularized ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and considering increasing amounts of regularization via ridge regression. We show theoretically that OLS probes amplify low-variance directions in activation space that have spurious correlations with the target feature, whereas regularization reduces influence from these directions. Empirically, we find in a toy transformer and Llama-2-7B that intervention faithfulness increases up to a point, and then decreases again, and that the optimal regularization strength leads to features bearing striking similarity (in both direction and variance) to those learned by optimizing for intervention outcomes directly. Together, these results provide mechanistic justification for regularizing regression probes.

arxiv:2611.20377.title: Halting in Recurrent Sequence Models
arxiv:2611.20377.abstract: Recurrent sequence models, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and state space models (SSMs), are often trained to emit an end-of-sequence (EOS) token when their output sequence is complete. During training, EOS is treated as another token without a special loss term or incentive. Although this training paradigm is widely used, it is not understood how models decide to output EOS. We study a minimal version of the EOS halting problem in which networks are trained to emit a given input sequence an instructed number of times, followed by EOS. We train tanh RNNs and linear SSMs on this task, finding that the RNNs encode the number of tokens left to copy in a linear subspace, of which two principal components capture most of the variation. Hidden states with the same remaining count converge to a shared representation regardless of their instructed repeat count. By modulating the hidden state using an affine transformation at the boundary between copied sequences, we shift the RNN's state to the representation shared by states with one fewer copy remaining. The unchanged network emits EOS one copy earlier while reproducing the shortened target sequence in 94.4% of new sequences, revealing that this representation causally determines the stopping time. In the SSMs, the difference between trajectories with different repeat counts is separated across two-dimensional rotation planes whose contributions to the EOS comparison cancel during copying and align near the stopping time. Rotating the planes independently removes most of the intended stopping while preserving the copied content, which shows that the stopping time depends on the planes' relative phases. These results identify two candidate primitives of EOS halting in recurrent models: a shared encoding of the number of remaining tokens in tanh RNNs and phase alignment across fixed rotations in linear SSMs.

arxiv:2611.20384.title: JointQ: Joint Scale-and-Integer Quantization for Large Language Models
arxiv:2611.20384.abstract: GPTQ is the de facto standard solver for layer-wise post-training quantization (PTQ) of large language models, yet the solver itself has received less attention than weight preprocessing and cross-layer objectives. We target a bottleneck of GPTQ: its greedy procedure optimizes continuous group scales separately from the assignment of discrete integers. Evaluating each integer candidate with its closed-form optimal scale has been used for per-channel quantization; JointQ extends it to group-wise quantization, where a row's scales are coupled through the Hessian, and applies it to refine the GPTQ solution. Each local-search move changes one integer and recomputes its group's optimal scale in closed form, accounting for the other groups through the full Hessian; all scales are periodically re-solved jointly. The search starts from a row-wise selection among scale-refitted candidates including the GPTQ solution, so unregularized JointQ never has a larger layer-wise calibration error than GPTQ. JointQ preserves the GPTQ output format and is thus a drop-in replacement. Across four models and four settings, JointQ improves six-task average zero-shot accuracy over vanilla GPTQ in 14 of 16 comparisons and perplexity in 12 of 16. The mean accuracy gain increases from 0.0044 in W4G128 to 0.1559 in W3 per-channel, and JointQ also improves average accuracy over GPTQ with MSE-based scale search and activation ordering in all eight per-channel comparisons, though rarely in G128. An ablation shows that JointQ's diagonal Tikhonov regularization mitigates severe W3 per-channel perplexity degradation, so the largest gains are not due to the local search alone. Overall, JointQ's primary empirical benefit is downstream accuracy preservation in challenging low-bit and large-group regimes. Code is available in the OneComp library at https://github.com/FujitsuResearch/OneCompression.

arxiv:2611.20390.title: Architectural Principles for Parameter-Efficient Unitary Transformations in Coherent Optical Neural Networks
arxiv:2611.20390.abstract: Coherent optical neural networks based on interferometric architectures offer a promising route toward high-throughput, energy-efficient computation by exploiting the multiple degrees of freedom of light, including spatial, temporal, and spectral modes. However, practical implementations are constrained by the number of tunable parameters due to fabrication complexity, device footprint, and control overhead. In such parameter-constrained settings, achieving high expressive power remains a central challenge. We identify two key architectural requirements for maintaining high expressive power under these constraints: (i) statistical uniformity in the implemented transformations and (ii) strong mixing capability per parameter, which enables rapid and unbiased redistribution of information across modes. To realize these requirements, we develop a logarithmic-depth butterfly-topology architecture whose fundamental building block is a single phase-shifter--beam-splitter pair, in contrast to conventional rectangular mesh architectures based on Mach-Zehnder interferometers. Computational evaluations show that, particularly at restricted parameter counts, the proposed architecture achieves lower matrix-reconstruction errors and higher classification accuracies than conventional meshes in both feedforward and recurrent networks. We further quantify these design principles using graph-theoretic measures, expected squared moduli of transformation-matrix entries, and matrix-reconstruction error. The resulting framework provides a quantitative and physically interpretable basis for parameter-efficient optical neural networks.

arxiv:2611.20403.title: Attention Sinks as Spectral Spikes: A Mechanism Analysis of Gated Attention
arxiv:2611.20403.abstract: Transformer attention exhibits attention sinks, where a small subset of source tokens absorbs disproportionate attention mass across layers. Recent work shows that post-SDPA output gating strongly reduces attention-sink behavior, while separate studies link attention sinks to gradient sinks and massive activations through backward training dynamics. Yet how the same gate affects forward sink structure, backward gradient concentration, and training-time representation signatures remains unclear. We address this gap by formulating attention sinks as sink-induced low-rank modes in token-space covariance, with directions aligned to high-mass attention columns. Under this view, post-SDPA gating acts as a mode-dependent contraction: it attenuates sink-induced spectral energy in the forward pass and locally reduces value-path gradients routed through sink columns in the backward pass. Empirically, random-matrix diagnostics show that gating reduces outlier mass, weakens sink-subspace alignment, and increases effective rank, while backward analyses show active-gate attenuation of first-token value gradients. Training-time diagnostics further show that gating suppresses the co-emergence of attention concentration, value-gradient amplification, and representation dominance.

arxiv:2611.20404.title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
arxiv:2611.20404.abstract: When high-quality data runs out, a common practice is to train on it for several epochs, but each repeat is worth less than the last. Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, is another way to spend that compute, yet it has not been tested against a vanilla Transformer that spends the same compute on more epochs. We run this test across a ladder of model sizes, unique data and epochs, tuning both models at every size and amount of unique data. Latent feedback makes every FLOP and every token count for more except when unique data is scarce relative to model size, a regime that today's models are far from. We find that latent feedback serves as an amplifier: with unique data fixed, it reaches a Transformer's loss with less compute; with epochs fixed, it reaches that loss with less unique data. Furthermore, both savings grow with unique data per parameter and with repetition, and downstream tasks agree. To go beyond our grid, we fit one scaling law to both models, in which latent feedback enters as a Transformer with more parameters; it predicts that both savings keep growing with unique data and repetition. Fitted on models from 60M to 271M parameters, the law predicts the losses at a held-out 778M size to within 0.3% and the gap between the two models to within 0.05%. At most, latent feedback saves 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. When data, not compute, is the limit, latent feedback is the better use of a FLOP for a model of a given size.

arxiv:2611.20417.title: When the Cheapest Feasible Router Fails: Auditing Deployment Commitments in Cost-Aware LLM Routing
arxiv:2611.20417.abstract: Cost-aware LLM routing often selects the cheapest policy meeting empirical risk and coverage constraints. Yet a router that passes an audit can violate its fixed service contract on new requests, even when candidate policies are constructed independently. We study this deployment-commitment decision with disjoint construction, audit, and test samples. Across 19 RouterBench task families, the cheapest audit-feasible router deploys in 91.82% of opportunities but violates the held-out contract in 32.22% of deployments. We introduce Menu-Aware Routing Commitment (MARC), which qualifies policies using audit evidence and a serving-cost tolerance to retain the apparent winner, deploy a supported alternative, or defer. Its practical policywise variant (MARC-P) reduces observed conditional failure to 0.73% at 85.79% deployment, with higher serving cost; fixed-margin and formal risk-control procedures provide competitive alternatives. Nested audits show how added evidence changes deployable policy sets, and learned semantic routing exhibits the same commitment failure. These results establish deployment commitment as a distinct operational decision connecting router evaluation, service reliability, and inference cost.

arxiv:2611.20419.title: Reasoning Again with a Quarter of the Experts: Retry First, Then Train
arxiv:2611.20419.abstract: Removing three quarters of the routed experts from a 122B-parameter reasoning mixture-of-experts model makes it fit in a 12 GiB file, and breaks it in a specific way: on LiveCodeBench it enters verbatim reasoning loops that run to the token limit on 44 of 120 development problems, where the unpruned model at the same 2-bit quantization loops on none. We study how much of that loss can be recovered without changing the kept experts' quantized bytes, in three steps of increasing cost. On development problems, a sampling penalty recovers part of it. Stopping a reply when it starts to loop and drawing again recovers more on top of it, with no weight change. Our method, B, adds rank-8 trained corrections to the kept experts, loaded as an adapter, and restores two experts per layer; it is fitted layer by layer to the unpruned model's expert block on the pruned model's own activations. In a pre-registered comparison on 130 easy and medium LiveCodeBench problems that no part of the study had touched, with both arms given the same sampling penalty and the same stop-and-redraw policy, B solves 116 problems against 104 (+9.2 pp, 95% CI [+3.1, +15.4]; 15 problems gained, 3 lost). A training-free weight edit aimed at the loops, tested the same way earlier, did not help. B removes more wrong answers than loops, and costs 1.7x the wall time. On two older benchmarks used as regression checks, B stays inside a pre-set 2 pp tolerance but shows no gain (HumanEval+ +0.6 pp, MBPP+ -1.9 pp). The evidence is one model, one quantization and one benchmark family; we state what it does and does not show.

arxiv:2611.20427.title: Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Navigation
arxiv:2611.20427.abstract: Continual robot navigation requires reinforcement learning policies to continuously adapt to new environments while retaining previously acquired knowledge. Meanwhile, explainable reinforcement learning aims to learn meaningful behavioral representations through policy interaction. However, these objectives are inherently conflicting, as continual learning emphasizes policy stability whereas explainable behavior learning requires adaptive exploration. Existing methods rarely address both simultaneously. To resolve this issue, this paper proposes a Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (FECHRL) method. A two-stage behavior cloning strategy is introduced to balance rapid policy adaptation and explainable behavior evolution by progressively transitioning from strong imitation guidance to autonomous reinforcement learning. Furthermore, a fuzzy critic based on a Takagi--Sugeno fuzzy inference system is proposed to alleviate value extrapolation errors during the transition between imitation-guided learning and autonomous exploration, thereby improving continual training stability. Experimental results on sequential multi-scenario navigation tasks demonstrate that the proposed method effectively unifies continual learning capability and policy explainability within a single reinforcement learning framework, achieving stable knowledge retention and meaningful behavioral explanation.

arxiv:2611.20430.title: TrainExplorer: Autonomous LLM Post-Training via Plan-and-Decouple Exploration
arxiv:2611.20430.abstract: LLM-based agents can automate model post-training, accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement. Despite their promise, existing approaches remain under-explored and face two main challenges: (1) strategy lock-in that limits exploration beyond the initial strategy; and (2) coupled execution that obscures the effects of individual modifications. To address these challanges, we propose TrainExplorer, a multi-agent framework for autonomous post-training, that incorporates strategy planning and execution decoupling, to achieve broaden strategy exploration. First, strategy planning draws on scientific literature to construct a candidate search space of training strategies. Then, decoupled execution enables single-component interventions and attribution to guide strategy exploration. Extensive experiments on PostTrainBench demonstrate that TrainExplorer achieves a weighted aggregate score of 39.02, outperforming Claude Code using the same LLM by 7.32 and surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol-powered Codex, which scores 36.23. Code will be available.

arxiv:2611.20435.title: iEEG Can Help EEG: Improving Clinical Scalp EEG Analysis through Intracranial Priors
arxiv:2611.20435.abstract: Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is a cornerstone of clinical brain monitoring, making the quality of its signal fundamental to downstream tasks and models. However, that signal is heavily contaminated by non-neural interference and blurred by volume conduction. Existing methods operate almost exclusively within the scalp modality, so they inherit the contamination they would need to overcome. In practice, intracranial EEG (iEEG) observes the neural activity with far higher fidelity, yet it is invasive and therefore scarce, and the two modalities are rarely recorded as pairs at scale, share no common channel space, and offer no clean ground truth to directly supervise a mapping. Motivated by the neuronal synchronization mechanism shared by the two modalities, we propose a reprogramming approach that fits a signal-to-signal model on iEEG alone and freezes it as a cross-modal prior. We introduce ReBrain, a framework to transfer an iEEG-learned prior to scalp EEG, which re-expresses any scalp signal through that prior and can be inserted upstream of any downstream model with no pairing or fine-tuning. ReBrain consistently improves host models across recordings from multiple hospitals and across architecture families, and our analysis traces this gain to genuine neural structure carried by iEEG rather than to the architecture itself. This work provides evidence that a scarce clean modality can serve as a transferable prior for an abundant noisy one, offering a general recipe for cross-modal transfer among biosignals. Our code is available at https://github.com/Xianglong-Bao/ReBrain.

arxiv:2611.20445.title: Explainable Federated Learning via Global-Local Attribution Alignment
arxiv:2611.20445.abstract: Federated learning enables on-device training without centralizing data, yet existing systems still struggle to provide explanations that are both locally faithful and globally consistent under strict privacy and bandwidth constraints. Prior approaches either keep explanations siloed across clients, transmit heavy or sensitive artifacts, or replace expressive task models with interpretable surrogates that sacrifice accuracy. We propose xFedAlign, a model-agnostic framework that decouples task optimization in parameter space from explanation coordination in a compact group space. Each client distills a lightweight surrogate to produce private, per-class top-k attribution artifacts, which are robustly aggregated by the server into a Global Explanation Prior that softly aligns client explanations without constraining task learning. Across image, text, and tabular benchmarks with IID and non-IID partitions, xFedAlign matches FedAvg accuracy while consistently reducing explanation drift and improving deletion and insertion AUC relative to Local-XAI, FedAttr-Agg, and Fed-XAI, with only a few kilobytes of additional communication per round. Privacy and robustness evaluations further demonstrate reduced membership inference advantage and increased resistance to attribution poisoning, enabling consistent and trustworthy explanations in federated learning.

arxiv:2611.20451.title: Generative AI-Driven Parametric Design Optimization Framework for Vehicle Closure Systems
arxiv:2611.20451.abstract: This study presents a generative AI-driven parametric design optimization framework integrating performance-oriented generation with editable computer-aided design (CAD) and downstream computer-aided engineering (CAE) analysis for industrial vehicle closure systems. The framework is demonstrated on an automotive tailgate assembly with complex geometry, coupled components, and competing performance and feasibility requirements. A production-oriented CATIA model is restructured into a reference-based parametric template with a 13-dimensional design representation. An automated CAD/CAE workflow generates parametric models, performs structural analysis, and constructs a database of mass, maximum displacement, and maximum von Mises stress. Gaussian process regression surrogates predict performance, while diffusion and flow matching models generate design candidates. The design problem minimizes mass and maximum displacement, with stress assessed as an engineering feasibility constraint. Performance-guided generation using surrogate guidance and performance-aware training using a performance-aware loss incorporate engineering objectives, with sensitivity to guidance scale and loss weight evaluated. Generative search is compared with NSGA-II under matched evaluation budgets using a common surrogate model. Selected Pareto-region candidates are reconstructed in CATIA and re-evaluated through native CAE; all verified candidates are successfully regenerated and analyzed. Relative to the baseline, the knee-point design reduces mass by 7.1% and maximum displacement by 29.4%, while extreme verified solutions achieve maximum reductions of 10.3% and 37.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate performance-oriented multi-objective design exploration compatible with editable industrial CAD and native engineering verification.

arxiv:2611.20464.title: AdaModalX: Synchronization-Free MFM Inference for Distributed Multimodal Mobile Sensing via Progressive Data Orchestration
arxiv:2611.20464.abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) support generalizable inference in distributed mobile sensing applications by integrating heterogeneous data streams. However, existing MFM inference pipelines typically require complete and synchronized multimodal inputs, whereas mobile sensing streams arrive asynchronously due to network variability and heterogeneous data volumes across modalities. Waiting for all modalities increases end-to-end latency, while inference with incomplete inputs can reduce accuracy. We argue that multimodal inference should depend on the utility of available information rather than modality completeness. Based on this principle, we propose AdaModalX, a progressive multimodal inference framework that decouples inference execution from modality synchronization through runtime utility-aware orchestration. At each device, importance-aware data uploading uses a lightweight probe distilled from the edge-side MFM to allow reliable samples to exit locally while uncertain samples continue uploading. At the edge, on-demand MFM activation constructs candidates from fully received samples and, when needed, imputed features derived from partially received delayed inputs. A lightweight contribution assessor built on frozen MFM encoders estimates candidate utility and activates the MFM once the candidate meets its corresponding utility threshold. Experiments on four mobile sensing applications show that AdaModalX improves the accuracy-latency trade-off, achieving up to 26.97% accuracy improvement and up to 64.75% end-to-end latency reduction.

arxiv:2611.20467.title: On the Applicability of $p$-adic Numbers in Computational Modules for Neural Networks
arxiv:2611.20467.abstract: The applicability of $p$-adic arithmetic as an intermediate computational module in an otherwise unchanged machine-learning pipeline is investigated. A one-feature linear regression on the scikit-learn Diabetes dataset serves as the test model. The fitted coefficients are represented in $\mathbb{Q}_p$, predictions are computed in that field, and rational reconstruction is applied to the outputs. In the pyAdic experiments, rational reconstruction either returns no result or produces values that differ from the baseline predictions; changing computational precision can change both the magnitude and sign of the reconstructed value. In SageMath, forward conversions succeed, but the reconstructed predictions differ from the baseline. An alternative representation based on digit reversal fails to preserve ordinary addition because of carry propagation. Under the tested settings, none of the test predictions is reconstructed correctly. These results show that the tested conversion and reconstruction procedures do not provide a compatible intermediate module even for linear regression. Models defined directly over $p$-adic data and operations offer a direction for further investigation.

arxiv:2611.20468.title: Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics
arxiv:2611.20468.abstract: Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. We compare TabPFN-3.5 with two DeepED baselines, $DeepED_{LSTM}$ and $DeepED_{Transformer}$, on CarbonGlobe's overall evaluation, which trains on a uniform 1/16 sample of sites and tests on the other 50,779, predicting the 40-year state of all seven ED outputs. We then test every model, trained on present-day data only, on ED runs forced by SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 for 2021--2060 in six continental forest regions. With no training, TabPFN-3.5 has the lowest present-day height error of the three models and is within 4% of $DeepED_{LSTM}$ for soil carbon, but is less accurate for AGB, LAI and the carbon fluxes. In 2060, errors are several times larger than at the same sites under present-day forcing, and every model underestimates the biomass that ED gains. Under SSP5-8.5, TabPFN-3.5 is the most accurate model for height, AGB, soil carbon and LAI, with the lowest AGB error in all six regions, although, unlike ED, it predicts no larger biomass gain than under SSP1-2.6. Under SSP1-2.6, no model is best overall.

arxiv:2611.20472.title: Model Immunization Beyond Condition Numbers: The Importance of Plateau Regions
arxiv:2611.20472.abstract: Harmful fine-tuning can rapidly compromise safety alignment in Large Language Models, underscoring the vulnerability of deployed models to post-release modification. While prior work motivates model immunization by inducing ill-conditioned curvature to slow harmful optimization, this approach is not scalable due to the high computational cost of Hessian estimation. We refine this paradigm by extending the theoretical framework to prioritize plateau regions alongside curvature. We further introduce an immunization algorithm based on efficient Hessian estimation and bounds on the extremal singular values of the Hessian. We demonstrate the proposed immunization framework in three applications: (i) Fine-tuning-as-a-service settings where benign user data may be mixed with poisoned harmful data, (ii) open-weight settings where an adversary can fine-tune on harmful-only data with varied training dynamics, and (iii) robust unlearning, where immunized models better resist relearning attacks after unlearning. Extensive experiments confirm that our approach achieves robust defense against adversarial fine-tuning while largely maintaining general utility and downstream trainability. Our code is available at https://github.com/minhquoc0712/BECON.

arxiv:2611.20493.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
arxiv:2611.20493.abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenance. The wafer lot size, arrival profile, and factory maintenance policy are used as static covariates. TCNA is applied to a selected set of simulated discrete-event throughput and turnaround time trajectories. The $TH$ and $TA$ time series predicted by TCNA, evaluated with the common $MAPE$, $MSE$, and $R^2$ measures, show comparable or higher accuracy relative to other model architectures, with similar parameter counts and epoch times; the TCNA model size and execution time are similar to those of other architectures such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer. Although time series predictions are less accurate than high-resolution simulations, they can be deployed at a much lower computational cost. The TCNA achieves orders-of-magnitude speedup over PDEVS simulation with an acceptable loss of accuracy, enabling frequent product scheduling, capacity planning, and maintenance planning.

arxiv:2611.20521.title: LINK: Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-Node Propagation Rule Learning for Traffic Kriging
arxiv:2611.20521.abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic kriging aims to reconstruct traffic time series at unobserved locations with no historical traffic observations by leveraging spatial and temporal dependencies across the road network. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approaches primarily rely on neighborhood aggregation to capture spatial dependencies, thereby modeling traffic interactions implicitly and making it difficult to accurately recover traffic magnitudes at locations without historical observations. To address this limitation, we propose LINK, a Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-node propagation rule learning paradigm for traffic Kriging. LINK introduces three key designs: 1) a propagation-centric traffic kriging paradigm that explicitly learns a shared node-to-node transition rule; 2) a context-aware Spectral Propagation Network that performs traffic-state propagation in both the spectral and time domains; and 3) TraffiKrig, a realistic traffic kriging benchmark that preserves heterogeneous road-segment characteristics and road-specific metadata while enabling systematic comparison of representative kriging methods under a unified metadata-enhanced setting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LINK achieves strong reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency. Compared with the strongest baseline on each subset, LINK achieves an average MAE reduction of 54.7% over original baselines. LINK also achieves substantial efficiency improvements, reducing training time by 66.5% and inference time by 86.6% compared with the fastest competing methods. Zero-shot experiments further demonstrate the transferability of the learned propagation rule across regions.

arxiv:2611.20524.title: GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention
arxiv:2611.20524.abstract: Latent KV cache compression reduces memory footprint by mapping historical keys and values into compact representations. However, generic compressed key states require reconstruction to native dimension before applying RoPE and computing attention scores, adding sequence-scaling overhead to the decode path. We characterize when a latent KV representation can serve directly as the execution state of pretrained RoPE. For RoPE-based transformers, exact static linear execution of the rotary key path requires the latent-to-native map to preserve the pretrained RoPE action through an intertwining relation, restricting exact mixing to coordinates that share the same RoPE frequency. Guided by this characterization, we build GaugeRoPE, a training-free executable latent KV representation. It combines a RoPE-compatible carrier that preserves the rotary action with an approximate position-independent residual key--value (RKV) correction for complementary key and value information, both evaluated without per-token dense historical K/V reconstruction. On Mistral-7B, GaugeRoPE achieves $5.85\times$ KV compression while maintaining quality close to the full-cache baseline. Additional MHA results validate the construction beyond GQA. GaugeRoPE achieves up to $2.48\times$ the decode throughput of the vanilla uncompressed baseline through direct latent execution.

arxiv:2611.20549.title: RoShift: Lazy Shift and Weight-aware Rotation for Activation Sparsity in LLM Inference
arxiv:2611.20549.abstract: Activation sparsity accelerates LLM decoding by skipping unnecessary weight reads and computation. However, SiLU-based LLMs exhibit little natural sparsity, and imposing high sparsity can substantially degrade accuracy. We propose RoShift, a training-free method that transforms activations into sparsity-friendly representations. RoShift introduces lazy shift, which recenters SiLU activation distributions around zero and defers correction to the end of the FFN to obtain additional sparsity. It also reduces sparsification-induced output error through rotation that jointly accounts for activation and weight information. By fusing the corrections required for shifting and rotation, RoShift translates these gains into decoding speedup. At 50% and 60% sparsity, RoShift improves average accuracy over TEAL by 1.60 and 3.29 percentage points, respectively, across five models. It achieves up to $1.72\times$ decoding speedup over the dense model on an RTX 5090 at 50% sparsity and yields a better accuracy-speedup Pareto frontier than TEAL. Code is available at https://github.com/hulahula3247/RoShift

arxiv:2611.20562.title: One-Shot Calibration via Model Editing
arxiv:2611.20562.abstract: Model editing aims to correct errors in large, pretrained models by replacing model generations with user-provided responses. Existing editors assume a single target answer for each edit. However, many real tasks inherently entail uncertainty, resulting in multiple plausible answers with varying likelihoods in user feedback. Such feedback forms a target distribution to not only correct but also calibrate model generations. We therefore propose SoftEdit, the first model editor to leverage uncertainty in user responses and perform one-shot calibration during editing. To generalize calibration to unseen samples, SoftEdit uses co-plausibility relationships between answers while preserving real distributional shifts, balancing the new distributional generality-locality tradeoff. Across three language models, three vision-language models, and two large datasets, SoftEdit achieves state-of-the-art performance, ultimately showing that uncertainty in user responses enables generalizable calibration of pretrained models beyond single-answer corrections.

arxiv:2611.20565.title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache
arxiv:2611.20565.abstract: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. We reduce this extra memory by quantizing the draft cache. The target cache and verifier remain in BF16, so that compression cannot change the target model's final correction rule. We first study how to divide precision between keys and values. A naive per-token quantizer makes keys appear much more sensitive: splitting a 12-bit budget, K8V4 beats K4V8 in acceptance by 10.87pp. However, with grouped per-channel keys, the gap becomes -0.25pp. A controlled Qwen test confirms that changing only the key quantizer can erase or reverse the preferred bit split. Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.

arxiv:2611.20567.title: Calibrated Functional Prediction from Overlapping Nonlinear Observations
arxiv:2611.20567.abstract: We study prediction of nonlinear audit functionals from scalar observations of a shared hidden table state. For Schur-rational operators, local Gaussian projections yield a common sparse kernel for overlapping tasks, repeated row identities, and cross-row dependence. Shared-state residual samples extend this kernel through a positive-semidefinite feature representation. Positive matrix integration and sample-value enclosures connect the original inputs to the actual saved hybrid prediction. A sorted calibration-role perturbation bound then certifies its complete finite-pool pinball risk. Independent complete-loss selection chooses the ridge, score scale, and residual weight, while task-rank calibration supplies an upper endpoint. Evaluation uses twenty new reference contexts per dataset at two task sizes, giving 400 conditions across ten benchmark populations. The mean dataset complete-loss ratios are 0.9977 to the degree-two kernel, 0.9961 to matched complete-MC shrinkage, and 0.9911 to the retrospective minimum over 174 public configurations. The last ratio has a paired reference-bootstrap interval of [0.9898,0.9927]. On 40 profiles at coefficient tolerance $10^{-7}$, Gamma quadrature has a geometric mean cold-time ratio of .0646 to strengthened Arb/Petras integration.

arxiv:2611.20602.title: Quantum Computing-Based Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks for Airfoil Parameterization
arxiv:2611.20602.abstract: Airfoil geometry parameterization is essential in aerodynamic design optimization. Optimization search in the large space suffers from low efficiency and modest feasible region, which could further incur failures to convergence. Generative adversarial networks (GAN), aiming to learn the statistical distribution of existing data, pave a new avenue for shape generation and airfoil parameterization. GAN manages to implicitly reduce design space by generating only smooth, realistic airfoils. Meanwhile, quantum computing has been emergingly exhibiting great potential for achieving superior performance in specific types of engineering problems but has not been introduced to airfoil parameterization. To fill this gap, this work develops quantum computing-based Wasserstein GAN (Q-WGAN) and investigates the performance for airfoil parameterization. The Q-WGAN adopts parameterized quantum circuits as the generator to promote the generative performance, while the discriminator remains classical. The developed Q-WGAN is demonstrated on a dataset of optimal airfoils parameterized by free-form deformation (FFD) control points, resulting from 992 airfoil aerodynamic design optimizations. Results show that Q-WGAN achieves 92.1% mean fitting accuracy on the optimal FFD control points and 99.2% accuracy on airfoil coordinates, comparable with the classical WGAN performance of 92.28% on FFD control points and 99.26% on airfoil coordinates. Q-WGAN achieves lower Jensen-Shannon divergence, Fr\'echet distance, and Wasserstein distance than the classical WGAN, indicating an improved agreement with the reference airfoil distribution. Therefore, this work presents a convincing evidence that Q-WGAN makes a viable option for parameterizing airfoils and possesses a great potential for other relevant engineering applications.

arxiv:2611.20607.title: DNA: A Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture for Industrial Digital Twin
arxiv:2611.20607.abstract: High-fidelity modeling is fundamental to industrial digital twin, yet a trade-off persists between the physical transparency of mechanistic models and the superior predictive power of data-driven approaches. Existing hybrid methods often fail to bridge this gap, suffering from shallow integration and rigid one-shot modeling strategies that struggle with complex industrial systems. To address these issues, we propose a \textbf{Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture (DNA)}. Inspired by the double-helix structure of biological \textit{DNA}, our architecture intertwines mechanistic and data-driven modeling strands through two novel interaction strategies, forming a symbiotic architecture in which the two strands mutually enhance predictive capability. Furthermore, the hierarchical structure of DNA allows it to model complex systems in a multi-stage manner through two tailored deep learning frameworks. We evaluate the proposed approach on two distinct industrial systems, where DNA achieves reductions in MAE of 3.704\% and 3.175\%, respectively, compared to the strongest baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DNA and suggest its potential to provide new insights for the development of industrial digital twins.

arxiv:2611.20609.title: Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs
arxiv:2611.20609.abstract: Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances.
